entries.title: Triple Point Technology Inc v PTT Public Company Ltd
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: Liquidated damages clauses are construed by their terms; the entitlement to liquidated damages accrues up to the date of termination, not beyond.
entries.facts: A dispute over liquidated damages in a software contract.
entries.holding: Liquidated damages clauses are construed by their terms; the entitlement to liquidated damages accrues up to the date of termination, not beyond.

entries.title: Wood v Capita Insurance Services Ltd
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: Interpretation is a unitary exercise: the court considers the language, the context and the commercial purpose, without privileging one over the other.
entries.facts: A dispute over the interpretation of an indemnity clause in a share purchase agreement.
entries.holding: Interpretation is a unitary exercise: the court considers the language, the context and the commercial purpose, without privileging one over the other.

entries.title: Arnold v Britton
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: Contractual interpretation begins with the natural and ordinary meaning of the words; commercial common sense cannot override clear language.
entries.facts: A dispute over service charges in a lease of holiday chalets.
entries.holding: Contractual interpretation begins with the natural and ordinary meaning of the words; commercial common sense cannot override clear language.

entries.title: Cavendish Square Holding BV v Talal El Makdessi
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: A penalty clause is unenforceable where it imposes a detriment out of proportion to any legitimate interest of the innocent party in performance, viewed as at the time of contracting.
entries.facts: A dispute over penalty clauses in a share purchase agreement.
entries.holding: A penalty clause is unenforceable where it imposes a detriment out of proportion to any legitimate interest of the innocent party in performance.

entries.title: Kenya Commercial Bank v Suntra Investment Bank
entries.principle: Commercial disputes are resolved on the evidence; the court will enforce contractual obligations and award damages for breach.
entries.note: Verify the neutral citation on Kenya Law before relying on it.

entries.title: Rainy Sky SA v Kookmin Bank
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: Where contractual language admits of two meanings, the court prefers the construction consistent with business common sense.
entries.facts: A dispute over the interpretation of a refund guarantee in a shipbuilding contract.
entries.holding: Where contractual language admits of two meanings, the court prefers the construction consistent with business common sense.

entries.title: Chartbrook Ltd v Persimmon Homes Ltd
entries.principle: The court may correct an obvious drafting error where the parties' objective intention is clear, applying the principle of construction against the draftsman.
entries.facts: A dispute over the meaning of a price formula in a development agreement.
entries.holding: The court may correct an obvious drafting error where the parties' objective intention is clear, applying the principle of construction against the draftsman.

entries.title: Investors Compensation Scheme Ltd v West Bromwich Building Society
entries.principle: Contractual interpretation seeks the meaning the document would convey to a reasonable person with the relevant background knowledge, giving effect to commercial common sense.
entries.facts: A dispute over the meaning of an indemnity clause in a compensation scheme.
entries.holding: Contractual interpretation seeks the meaning the document would convey to a reasonable person with the relevant background knowledge, giving effect to commercial common sense.
